test_title: PYST 10 - SSC CHSL 2025 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On: 15 Nov, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: Two vertical poles stand on the ground, 50 meters apart. The height of the smaller pole is 10 meters. From the top of the smaller pole, the angle of elevation of the top of the taller pole is 30º. Find the height of the taller pole.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Height of taller pole (H) = Height of smaller pole (h) + distance × tan(θ)

H = 10 + 50 × tan(30º)

H = 10 + 50 × (1 / √3) ≈ 10 + 50 × 0.57735

H = 10 + 28.87 = 38.87 m

**∴ The correct answer is 38.87 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Height of smaller pole (AB) = 10 m

Distance between poles (BD) = 50 m

Angle of elevation from top of smaller pole (θ) = 30º

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/42c3daa231f45fa012beab01ec7e71f71567651efa2231ac8555491444f76275.png] 

Let the taller pole be CD and the smaller pole be AB.

From the figure, AB = ED = 10 m and AE = BD = 50 m.

In right-angled triangle AEC:

⇒ tan(30º) = CE / AE

⇒ 1 / √3 = CE / 50

⇒ CE = 50 / √3

⇒ CE = 50 / 1.732

⇒ CE ≈ 28.87 m

Total height of the taller pole (CD) = CE + ED

⇒ CD = 28.87 + 10

⇒ CD = 38.87 m

**∴ The correct answer is 38.87 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle of Elevation

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when an object is viewed above the horizontal level.

Trigonometric Ratios

In a right-angled triangle, tan θ = Perpendicular / Base. Common value: tan 30º = 1/√3 ≈ 0.577, tan 45º = 1, tan 60º = √3 ≈ 1.732.

Angle of Depression

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when an object is viewed below the horizontal level.</p
